title: Iteration reaches zero measure
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $g:\alpha\to\alpha$, let $I$ be a property on $\alpha$, and let $\mu:\alpha\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose $I$ is preserved by $g$, that whenever $I(s)$ and $0<\mu(s)$ hold the measure strictly decreases under $g$, and that whenever $I(s)$ and $\mu(s)=0$ hold, $g(s)=s$. Then for every natural number $n$ and every $s$ satisfying $I(s)$ and $\mu(s)\le n$, the measure after applying $g$ exactly $n$ times to $s$ is zero.
hypotheses_covered: Fixing points of measure zero satisfying $I$
